name: Amber Fort
why: Jaipur's grandest fort: honey-coloured walls, mirror halls and lake views.
history: Amer was the capital of the Kachhwaha rulers before Jaipur was built. Raja Man Singh I began the main palace in the late 16th century, and later rulers kept adding courtyards and halls. It's part of the 'Hill Forts of Rajasthan' UNESCO World Heritage site.
bestTime: Right at opening, around 8 am, before the heat and the tour buses
crowdTip: Tour groups arrive from about 10 am. Go first thing and do the Sheesh Mahal before anything else.
angleTip: Skip the main gate selfie. From the lakeside garden road below, the whole fort stacks up beautifully in the water.

name: Jaigarh Fort
why: The tough, military fort on the ridge above Amer, with a giant cannon and huge views.
history: Built in the early 18th century under Sawai Jai Singh II to protect Amer, Jaigarh was a working military fort with a cannon foundry. It holds the Jaivana, one of the largest wheeled cannons in the world. A walled path links it to Amer below.
bestTime: Morning, straight after Amber Fort, or late afternoon
crowdTip: Much quieter than Amer. The road up is steep, so take a cab or jeep rather than walking in the heat.
angleTip: Walk to the ramparts facing Amer: you get the whole fort and the lake from above, with no one in your frame.

name: Panna Meena ka Kund
why: A small, perfect stepwell with criss-cross stairs, ten minutes from Amber Fort.
history: This stepwell in Amer is believed to date to around the 16th century. It collected rainwater for the town and was a cool place to rest and meet. Its zig-zag staircases on three sides make it one of Jaipur's most photographed spots.
bestTime: Early morning, 7–9 am, for soft light and fewer people
crowdTip: Climbing the steps is often not allowed now; respect the caretakers and photograph from the edge.
angleTip: Shoot from a corner rather than the centre: the diagonal stairs look like a woven pattern.

name: Hawa Mahal
why: The 'Palace of Winds': a pink honeycomb of windows right on the bazaar.
history: Built in 1799 under Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh, Hawa Mahal let royal women watch street life and processions without being seen. Its many small jharokha windows also keep air moving. It's really a tall screen wall, only a room or so deep at the top.
mustSee: Top floors and their tiny windows
View over the bazaar towards Jantar Mantar
bestTime: Early morning for the façade in soft light; go inside right at opening
crowdTip: The road in front is busy all day. See the façade early, then explore inside before groups arrive.
angleTip: Climb to a first-floor café across the road for the façade from eye level, with no traffic in front.

name: City Palace
why: The heart of Jaipur, still home to the royal family, with painted gates and a fine textile gallery.
history: Sawai Jai Singh II began the City Palace when he founded Jaipur in 1727. Later rulers added halls, courtyards and gardens. Part of it is still a royal residence; the rest is a museum.
mustSee: Peacock Gate in Pritam Niwas Chowk
crowdTip: The four painted gates get crowded around noon. Go there first, then the galleries.
angleTip: Photograph one painted gate detail up close instead of the whole courtyard; the peacocks are hand-painted feather by feather.

name: Jantar Mantar
why: A giant stone observatory that tells time with shadows, and actually works.
history: Built in the 1720s and 1730s by Sawai Jai Singh II, a ruler fascinated by astronomy. Its huge masonry instruments track time, the sun and the stars. It's a UNESCO World Heritage site, and the big sundial is one of the largest in the world.
bestTime: A sunny morning, so the shadows are sharp
crowdTip: There's little shade. Go before noon and carry water. A guide or audio guide really helps here.
angleTip: Lie your phone low and shoot the sundial's shadow edge creeping along the marble scale.

name: Nahargarh Fort
why: The best sunset over the Pink City, from a fort on the ridge.
history: Built in 1734 under Sawai Jai Singh II as a retreat and part of the city's defences. Later, the Madhavendra Bhawan was added, a set of matching suites for the queens joined by corridors.
crowdTip: Weekends at sunset get busy. Go on a weekday and arrive an hour before sunset. Arrange your ride back down in advance.
angleTip: Skip the packed main viewpoint and find a quieter wall: the city lights coming on below are the real show.

name: Albert Hall Museum
why: Rajasthan's oldest museum, in a grand building that glows at night.
history: The foundation stone was laid in 1876 during the Prince of Wales's visit, and the building opened as a museum in 1887. It was designed by Samuel Swinton Jacob in the Indo-Saracenic style. Inside are crafts, carpets, armour and a well-known Egyptian mummy.
bestTime: Afternoon inside, then stay for the lights at dusk
crowdTip: Quiet on weekday afternoons. Evening crowds gather outside for the lights, not inside.
angleTip: Walk into Ram Niwas Garden and shoot back through the trees: arches, lamps, no traffic.

name: Chand Baori
why: One of India's deepest and most dramatic stepwells: a day trip worth the drive.
history: Chand Baori in Abhaneri village dates to around the 9th century and is linked to a local ruler, Raja Chanda. Around 3,500 narrow steps fall about 13 levels to the water, built to save water in a dry land. The Harshat Mata temple stands next to it.
bestTime: Morning: leave Jaipur around 7 am and arrive before the heat
timeNeeded: Half day with the drive (about 2–2.5 hours each way)
crowdTip: You can't walk down the steps; you view from the galleries. Pair it with a road-side lunch on the way back.
angleTip: Go to a back corner of the gallery and shoot straight down: the steps turn into pure geometry.

name: Sanganer & Bagru printing villages
why: See hand-block printing where it's actually made, from carving to drying in the sun.
history: Printing families, often from the Chhipa community, have worked in Sanganer and Bagru for generations. Sanganer is known for fine florals on light grounds, Bagru for earthy natural dyes and dabu mud-resist. Long sheets drying in the fields are part of the scenery.
bestTime: Weekday mornings, when the printing tables are busiest
crowdTip: Big showrooms on the main road may call themselves workshops. Ask to see printing in progress before you shop.
angleTip: Shoot hands, not faces: a block mid-press, or a row of blocks on a shelf. Always ask first.
